name: House Targaryen
description: House Targaryen's succession crisis is overtaken by a larger dynastic threat. Baelenys still intends Jacaelon to succeed him, while Gaelor returns from Driftmark long enough to kill Brant Costayne in trial by combat and then plans a new Stepstones campaign from Essos. In the shadows, Vahaemon is revealed alive and preparing in Tyrosh with Vaenarr, Visenya, his son Aegor and multiple dragons. Aegor rides Sunfyre and is already known as the Young Dragon. The same chapter reopens an older wound: Baelenys remembers Aenys II forcing the disabled Malaenar to crawl before ordering Sheepstealer to kill his small dragon.

name: House Tyrell
description: Renrose Tyrell remains committed to Visenor's plan to destroy House Gardener and seize advantage from the Crown's response. Visenor returns to Oldtown convinced their alliance is secure, but Leo's trust has fractured: the boy follows him there, notices the suspicious work with Almar and secretly searches the maester's private chambers. The alliance now carries a hidden internal witness who may understand more than either side expects.

name: House Hightower
description: House Hightower remains broken but politically dangerous through what it shelters. In Oldtown, Melessa continues protecting Visenor while Maester Almar helps him complete a forged letter designed to frame House Gardener as Vahaemon's ally. A raven reporting a dragon and burned men near Starfall shifts Visenor's attention toward Dorne, while Leo Tyrell quietly slips into Almar's private chambers and begins searching his papers.

name: House Stark
description: Wardens of the North, bound to the Iron Throne by an old, uneasy loyalty sealed in blood generations ago. Lord Brandon Stark's death brought his son Rickard to Winterfell's seat, and House Targaryen back to its gates. That connection has since grown more personal: Rickard has begun openly courting Princess Saera Targaryen at Winterfell. In a gesture steeped in the old symbols of his house, he presented her with a white direwolf pup — a rare creature whose arrival has drawn the princess still further into the strange, ancient world of the North.

name: House Dayne
description: House Dayne is pulled into a new mystery around Starfall. Rhaella and the younger maester Nymos are both reported missing, burned bodies lie along the coast and an unburned basket matching Rhaella's has been found nearby. Lord Darren remains in Sunspear while Lorenah quietly mobilizes her father's men from King's Landing. Alester, meanwhile, returns from Winterfell and finally admits to Jace how deeply Saera's promise to Rickard Stark has affected him.

name: House Velaryon
words: The Old, the True, the Brave
description: Masters of Driftmark and the Crown's oldest maritime allies, tied now to the royal family directly through Naella Velaryon's marriage to Prince Gaelor. Naella carries his heir.

name: House Baratheon
description: Proud stormlanders who fought beside House Targaryen in the past and expect the debt remembered. The Young Stag, Steffon Baratheon, has learned that pride alone does not move a king — though he won the grand tourney by default when neither Targaryen prince could stand.

name: House Vance
description: House Vance of Atranta, a lesser house known mainly through Ser Brannyn Vance's service in the Kingsguard.

name: House Morrigen
description: A Reach house represented at court by Ser Orwell Morrigen, Lord Commander of the Kingsguard, who watches the realm's unraveling with growing unease.

name: House Lannister
description: Represented at court by Tion Lannister, the Master of Coin, whose sound financial counsel is consistently overruled by princes eager for war.

name: House Blackwood
description: A Riverlands house represented at the grand tourney by Lord Godfrey Blackwood, whose easy charm and open unconventionality made him as memorable off the lists as on them. His quarter-final loss to Jacaelon cost him nothing but pride; his instincts in the semi-finals, when he tackled Brant Costayne mid-assassination, likely saved Prince Gaelor's life.

name: House Mullendore
description: A minor Reach house whose sigil bears butterflies and whose seat lies in the Uplands. House Mullendore has served the Hightowers loyally for generations, and it is through that loyalty that Ser Martyn Mullendore came to recognize a disguised Visenor Targaryen bleeding in an Oldtown alley — and chose to deliver him to Lady Melessa rather than the Watch.

name: House Whent
description: A crownlands house best known here through Curtass Whent, whose long shadow stretched from the Kingsguard to the woods south of King's Landing. Word of his death there, killed in the King's service while hunting Prince Visenor, has since reached the Red Keep — received by the Crown with far more indifference than House Whent might have hoped for.

name: House Strong
description: A minor Riverlands house whose name survives at court through Baran Strong. Once a knight of the Kingsguard, Baran has since been cast from the white cloak and into exile, leaving his house's place in the affairs of the realm tied largely to his uncertain fate.

name: House Bracken
description: An ancient Riverlands house and bitter rival of House Blackwood. In 99 AC, men sworn to Lord Perric Bracken killed a Blackwood cousin near the disputed border, reopening a feud old enough that few remember its beginning. The bloodshed has since grown into a matter for the Hand of the King, with neither house inclined to yield.

name: House Tully
description: Lords Paramount of the Trident, charged with keeping peace among the proud and quarrelsome houses of the Riverlands. Under Lord Clover Tully, whose passive rule has done little to restrain his bannermen, that peace has grown increasingly brittle. His grandson's recent marriage into House Bracken has further complicated the ancient Bracken-Blackwood feud and raised questions over Riverrun's impartiality.

name: House Arryn
description: Lords of the Vale and one of the great houses of the realm. The Arryns have so far remained largely removed from the crises consuming the Crown, though their position, armies, and ancient prestige ensure that their allegiance cannot be ignored as divisions within House Targaryen deepen.

name: House Greyjoy
description: The ruling house of the Iron Islands, a land whose relationship with the Iron Throne has long been written in salt, steel, and blood. Memories of King Baelenys' wars in the islands remain vivid, not least the tale of his confrontation with Harrik, the towering warrior remembered as the Drowned Servant.

name: House Martell
description: Dorne responds quickly to reports that several men were burned near the Starfall coast, publicly circulating the sighting so the realm cannot later accuse it of concealing a dragon. The incident draws attention back toward House Dayne's lands just as Rhaella and Maester Nymos disappear, while Lord Darren Dayne remains in Sunspear.

name: House Gardener
description: House Gardener is now the target of an active frame-up. Visenor and Almar complete a false letter in Vahaemon's name claiming Gardener gold funds sellswords, western ports are being prepared for invasion and Vhagar has been found near Volantis. Almar believes Lord Gardener may already be travelling quietly toward King's Landing, making the timing of the forgery urgent.

name: House Karstark
description: An ancient northern house descended from House Stark, founded when Karlon Stark was granted lands for putting down a rebel lord more than a thousand years ago. From Karl's Hold came Karhold, and from its Stark lords came the Karstarks. Though bound to Winterfell by blood as well as fealty, they have grown over the centuries into one of the North's principal houses in their own right.

name: House Mooton
description: An old and wealthy Riverlands house seated at Maidenpool, whose lands command an important port on the Bay of Crabs. Though sworn beneath Riverrun, the Mootons possess wealth and influence disproportionate to their place in the feudal order, making Maidenpool a valuable prize whenever the politics of the Trident begin to fracture.

name: House Harlaw
description: Among the oldest, wealthiest, and most powerful houses of the Iron Islands, the Harlaws rule their island from Ten Towers beneath the overlordship of House Greyjoy. Their strength, lands, and numerous cadet branches make them a power in their own right, and one whose support can carry considerable weight whenever the captains and lords of the isles are divided.

name: House Celtigar
description: An ancient Valyrian house of Claw Isle, House Celtigar shares with the Targaryens and Velaryons a lineage reaching back to the Freehold. Wealthy by the standards of the Crownlands and traditionally bound to Dragonstone and the Iron Throne, the Celtigars remain one of the realm's surviving houses of Valyrian blood.

name: House Corbray
description: House Corbray is represented at court by Ser Lucas Corbray, the Kingsguard known as the Mustang. His affection for Princess Vhaemys repeatedly makes him too indulgent: Jace catches him helping her evade the spirit of a kitchen punishment and reminds him that friendship with a princess cannot outrank a white-cloak oath.

name: House Reyne
description: The family of Reyenald Reyne, a thirteen-year-old swordsman training under Orwell Morrigen at the Red Keep.
